# Ahmed Harbi Elsayed

> Robotics Researcher at DFKI (German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence) and PhD candidate at Osnabrück University, working on Explainable AI for marine and underwater robotic systems. Holds an MSc. in Marine and Maritime Intelligent Robotics from Toulon University (France) and Jaume I University (Spain).

Research areas: marine and underwater robotics (AUVs, ROVs, autonomous surface vehicles), computer vision and SLAM (visual odometry, underwater multi-camera deep SLAM), Explainable AI (XAI) for aquatic environments, human-robot collaboration, and Unity-based robotics simulation. Works primarily in Python, C++, and MATLAB with ROS1/ROS2, Unity, Docker, SolidWorks, and Ansys CFD.

Name variants used in publications and across the web: Ahmed Harbi Elsayed, Ahmed H Elsayed, Ahmed Harbi, Ahmed Elsayed.

## Selected projects

- [UnityUWSIM - Underwater Simulator](https://github.com/ahmedharbii/UnityUWSIM): Unity underwater simulator based on the CIRTESU Lab environment, featuring BlueROV2, docking stations, obstacles, and marine life. Used as the competition platform for the 2nd MIR Annual Symposium Robotics Challenge at UJI, Spain (2023).
- [Interactive Simulator Framework for XAI]({{ '/projects.html' | absolute_url }}): Interactive simulator framework for Explainable AI applications in aquatic environments, developed at DFKI.
- [UJI Butler]({{ '/projects.html' | absolute_url }}): Sign language recognition with YOLOv7 driving a UR5 robot arm and a Kobuki mobile robot in a coffee-serving task.
- [Deep Visual Odometry (DVO)]({{ '/projects.html' | absolute_url }}): Synthetic dataset collection pipeline in Unity plus deep visual odometry on BlueROV2 for underwater navigation (MSc project, 2023).
- [Autonomous Surface Vehicle (ASV)]({{ '/projects.html' | absolute_url }}): Autonomous DDBoat for open-water trajectory following. 1st place at the MIR Championship, Lac de Guerlédan, France (2022).
